standard_prerequisites: The situation defining the functor classifying the points where a module is flat in dimensions at least n, and the chart lemma reducing the functor to a quasi-affine situation over the base
The sheaf property for the fpqc topology and limit preservation in that quasi-affine situation
The behaviour of fpqc coverings and of filtered limits of affine schemes under base change
core_obligations: Part one: for an fpqc covering of a scheme over the base, choose the chart supplied by the chart lemma and identify the value of the functor on a test scheme with the value of the chart functor on the fibre product
Conclude the sheaf property because the base changed covering is again an fpqc covering and the chart functor has the sheaf property

Part two: given a filtered limit of affine schemes over the base where the functor is nonempty, choose the chart, pick an affine open of the fibre product mapping surjectively onto a stage, and take inverse images to obtain a filtered limit of affine schemes over the chart

Use the identification of the functor with the chart functor on fibre products to see that the chart functor is nonempty at the limit, apply limit preservation there, and conclude that the functor is nonempty at some stage
proof_roadmap: Reduce both assertions to the chart functor through the chart lemma
For the sheaf property use that base change of an fpqc covering is an fpqc covering
For limit preservation replace the filtered limit by a filtered limit of affine schemes over the chart and apply limit preservation there
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the sheaf property and limit preservation of the flatness-in-dimensions function at source lines 2121-2130, label lemma-flat-dimension-n, whose proof occupies source lines 2132-2166. Neither part is a citation: for the sheaf property the proof chooses the chart of the chart lemma and identifies the value of the functor on a test scheme with the value of the chart functor on the fibre product, which converts an fpqc covering into an fpqc covering of that fibre product and lets the chart case be applied. For limit preservation it has to manufacture the right limit: it picks an affine open of the fibre product mapping surjectively onto a stage and takes inverse images to obtain a filtered limit of affine schemes over the chart, after which the identification of the two functors and limit preservation in the chart case give the conclusion. The counted statement records neither the chart reduction nor the construction of the limit.
